definition: A 7B Qwen2.5 base checkpoint, and the archive's default subject for RLVR training experiments — small enough to train repeatedly, strong enough for the results to matter. It appears across the entropy work that established the reward-entropy exponential exchange, in token-selection studies, in adaptive compute allocation, and as one of the base models whose pass@k overtakes its own RLVR-trained descendant as k grows. Being a base rather than instruction-tuned checkpoint is why it recurs: the zero-RL setting, applying RL directly to a pretrained model, is what several archived sources use to isolate what RLVR contributes, and this is the model they use it on.

evidence.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
evidence.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

evidence.note: Turns token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps into turn-level credit for agentic RL by recursively updating a Bayesian belief in log-odds space, identifying pivotal turns without a critic.
evidence.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
evidence.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

evidence.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
evidence.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

evidence.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
evidence.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

evidence.note: Argues that Shannon entropy is the wrong criterion for picking which tokens to train on in RLVR, and selects tokens instead by the Jensen-Shannon divergence of their logit distribution from the group average, updating only the top 10% of these 'unique' tokens.
evidence.title: Beyond Entropy: Learning from Token-Level Distributional Deviations for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
evidence.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

evidence.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
evidence.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

evidence.note: Separates reasoning into procedural advancement and 'epistemic verbalization' — the token-level externalization of uncertainty — and shows that emitting doubt is what lets a model recover from silent divergence, that injecting a bare doubt cue recovers failed trajectories, and that 800 SFT examples suffice to install or destroy the habit.
evidence.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

evidence.note: Shows that greedy decoding is not deterministic across hardware: changing GPU type, GPU count or evaluation batch size shifts a reasoning model's AIME'24 accuracy by up to 9 percentage points and its response length by 9,000 tokens under BF16, because floating-point addition is non-associative.
evidence.title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference

evidence.note: Proves that an entropy bonus permanently moves the stationary point of RL training while covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once its coefficient is annealed, and that the bonus shrinks the stability margin where the targeted methods leave it intact.
evidence.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

name: Qwen2.5-7B
